name: V* Bench
ability_definition: The ability to see details at close range (within a few feet of the observer).

task_realism.reasoning: Finding and characterizing tiny, low-salience objects in high-resolution photos does exercise fine-detail perception. The core demand, resolving detail that is invisible from a coarse view, is the heart of near vision. But the tasks are generic natural scenes from SA-1B (the colour of a small cup, the material of a distant sign). Workplace near-vision tasks look different: reading fine print, inspecting solder joints or stitching, checking labels, examining specimens, spotting defects on parts. The benchmark rarely involves text, markings, or fine structure, which dominate real near-vision work.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Controlled high resolution with very small targets (under 0.05% of the image) makes it hard to solve the task from a downsampled view, which is a genuine strength. Search and zoom strategies loosely mimic a worker leaning in or picking up a magnifier. Still, inputs are static, pre-captured images with no control over lighting, angle, or distance. There is no time pressure, no consequence for errors, and no workflow context. Real near-vision work involves active, sustained inspection of physical objects, often under variable conditions.

construct_coverage.reasoning: The benchmark covers only two question types: attribute recognition (mostly colour and material) and relative position of small objects, across 191 images. It omits reading small text, discriminating fine textures or markings, detecting subtle defects, precise measurement, and sustained close inspection. The small item count also limits how well it samples the ability. Relative-position questions lean partly on spatial reasoning rather than acuity.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are real photographs, which beats synthetic grids. However, the outputs are forced multiple-choice selections among a few options. Real work produces other outputs: read-out values, pass/fail inspection judgments, located defects, transcribed text, or actions. Multiple choice also permits elimination strategies and chance-level guessing that real tasks do not allow.

transferability_reasoning: V* Bench is a well-designed probe of whether a vision system can resolve tiny details in high-resolution imagery, and its resolution controls make it a credible stand-in for fine-detail acuity. However, its natural-scene content, narrow attribute and position question types, small size, and multiple-choice format leave a large gap from workplace near-vision tasks such as reading fine print, inspecting components, or detecting subtle defects. Strong V* scores therefore indicate a necessary but far from sufficient component of real near-vision capability.

2023.model_or_system: SEAL (LLaVA-7B-based MLLM with the V* LLM-guided visual search module)
2023.human_reference: General adult workforce with normal or corrected-to-normal near vision, inspecting high-resolution images for small object details

2024.model_or_system: SEAL (V* guided visual search + Vicuna-7B MLLM)
2024.human_reference: General adults with normal or corrected near vision, viewing the full-resolution image on a screen and free to zoom and pan.
